scope: Resident Atari AES/GEM architecture with common VDI and BIOS/DOS context; detailed external and alternate implementations excluded.

claims.statement: Resident components are connected by ordinary calls, shared layouts, traps and callbacks.
APPL execution records and DOS process identity have separate fields and restoration roles.
Current execution and UI input/menu targets are separately represented.
AES dispatch runs synchronously through the trap and reaches scheduling on ordinary return.
A distinct resident APPL executes the screen-manager event loop.
Allocation, open visibility, content/frame responsibility and deletion are separate boundaries.
Clipped tree traversal expands objects into multiple semantic VDI operations.
Interrupt deferral, per-context event state, buffered messages and scheduling are separate stages.
Forms keep blocked call state while menus retain registered live trees and have an indirect tracking path.
Loaded and caller-fixed resources bind through the caller global array; free ends storage lifetime.
UPDATE is recursive and waitable; mouse control additionally changes routing.
Scheduler reentry, context-switch gating, timer privilege gating and local interrupt masks are distinct.
Workstations retain attributes and dispatch pointers, while target drivers and some buffers are shared.
Output and raster routines dispatch through device functions; selected CPU implementation is not a general driver completion contract.
AES dispatch, frames, menus and application callbacks create indirect edges.
BIOS/DOS support, resident AES initialization, UI cleanup and execution-record departure have distinct roles.

validation.method: Hash-pinned files, normalized selected ranges, structural markers and call-order checks, manual source reading and local links.
validation.limits: Structural checks verify locators/markers, not semantic equivalence, exhaustive control flow or runtime behavior.

resource_impact.includes: guards, alignment and unused reserved capacity
